A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWIFT study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-F. Moved and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original SWIFT evaluations, SSL baseline experiments, temperature analyses, and component ablations across five datasets.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds threshold, classifier-initialization, retrieval-quantity, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The three-stage procedure, text-initialized classifier, retrieval augmentation, confidence temperature, and learnable loss temperatures remain unchanged. The appendix pseudocode is also retained; renaming SWIFT and testing additional SSL variants do not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate semi-Aves, Aircraft, Cars, EuroSAT, and DTD, using LAION-400M retrieval data. The added analyses reuse existing classification coverage; they introduce no new dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: V2 newly evaluates FreeMatch against FixMatch, with and without temperatures, in Figure 13; v1 only cited FreeMatch. V2 also drops comparator configurations such as scaled-text initialization from the five-dataset linear-probing comparison in v1 Table 6. The main benchmark comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New analyses vary retrieval caps from 100 to 1,000 images per class, test very small confidence thresholds, and measure pseudo-label accuracy and its product with utilization. V2 Table 4 tests initialization within full stage-2 SWIFT, replacing v1 Table 5's comparison without stage-2 temperatures. Core benchmark splits, shot counts, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic analyses: separate temperature effects in Figure 3C, pseudo-label quality in Figure 7, post-initialization softmax distributions in Figure 11, and small/adaptive thresholds in Figures 12-13. Tables 6 and 11 add cost and retrieval-quantity analyses. Conversely, the detailed initialization comparisons in v1 Tables 5-6 are trimmed or replaced.

E5.justification: The three-seed loss-temperature study and standard-deviation reporting are retained from v1 Figure 11 as v2 Figure 14. No new repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice is reported for the added experiments.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores remain unchanged, including SWIFT's 71.5/76.3/79.7% averages. However, v2 adds substantial diagnostic results, initialization controls, resource measurements, and retrieval-scale results: Table 11 reports SWIFT rising from 66.2% to 69.7% across 100-1,000 retrieved images per class. Some earlier initialization results disappear. Tables 3/9 also retain incremental-gain annotations that no longer match adjacent rows after intermediate rows are removed.

T1.justification: The classifier, softmax, and supervised, pseudo-label, and retrieval loss equations remain mathematically equivalent. V2 largely presents previously displayed equations inline; no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the stated resource scope from VLM pretraining data to open-world data generally and presents temperatures as the headline remedy, whereas v1 explicitly paired them with classifier initialization. The central SSFSL contribution, approximately five-point advantage, and comparison with supervised learning remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of why small/adaptive thresholds can improve utilization yet fail without loss-temperature scaling. It softens the leakage assertion from no risk to reduced risk, but removes the explicit caveat that temperature tuning does not help DINOv2. Figure 1 and Table 2 also increasingly attribute combined initialization-and-temperature gains to temperatures alone.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from an A100 with 40GB to an RTX 4090 with 24GB, and Table 6 adds training-time and storage measurements. Appendix F removes the Python 3.8.19 and PyTorch 2.0.1 versions while retaining a greater-than-40GB GPU-memory recommendation. Core hyperparameters, code-access information, and licensing remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on robust finetuning, LiDAR auto-annotation, open-world instance detection, Alpha-CLIP, and visual prompt tuning. It explicitly connects classifier learning to Kumar et al.'s finetuning work. The overall positioning against existing SSL and FSL approaches remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten around temperature-based finetuning and open data. Classifier initialization moves into the stage-wise method description, terminology changes, and the appendix analysis and detailed-results sections exchange order.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format and substantially redesigns displays. Figure 1 is simplified, Figures 3 and 7 gain panels, and the backbone and initialization tables are reorganized or combined. New diagnostic figures and cost/retrieval tables accompany extensive relocation and caption revisions.

improvement.justification: The new temperature and threshold controls, retrieval-scale study, and cost comparison better support the mechanism and expose practical tradeoffs. These provide a limited net improvement despite unchanged benchmark performance. The gains are tempered by removed initialization comparisons and the DINOv2 temperature caveat, reduced software-version documentation, and inconsistent incremental-gain annotations in Tables 3/9.
